questions.question: Leo builds a number with base ten blocks on his desk: 4 thousand cubes, 2 hundred flats, 6 ten rods and 3 single ones. What is his number in standard form?
questions.explain: Each kind of block names one place, in order: thousands, hundreds, tens, ones, so 4 thousands 2 hundreds 6 tens 3 ones is 4263. The usual trap is putting the digits in the wrong places — count the blocks from the biggest to the smallest every time.

questions.question: Nia puts out base ten blocks for her number: 5 thousand cubes, 0 hundred flats, 8 ten rods and 1 single one. What is her number in standard form?
questions.explain: With no hundred flats you still need a 0 to hold the hundreds place, so the number is 5081. The most common mistake is leaving the zero out and writing 581, which changes the 5 from thousands into hundreds.

questions.question: On a place value chart, Amir writes 6 in the thousands column, 1 in the hundreds column, 5 in the tens column and 0 in the ones column. How is this number written in word form?
questions.explain: Read the chart in order — 6 thousands, 1 hundred, 5 tens, 0 ones — which says six thousand one hundred fifty. The trap is reading the 5 tens as 5 ones and saying ‘one hundred five’; 5 in the tens column always means fifty.

questions.question: Priya shows a number with 2 thousand cubes, 9 hundred flats, 0 ten rods and 4 single ones. Which expanded form matches her blocks?
questions.explain: Expanded form shows what each digit is worth, so 2 thousands is 2000, 9 hundreds is 900, and 4 ones is 4, giving 2000 + 900 + 4. The trap is writing the digits alone (2 + 9 + 0 + 4) instead of their values.

questions.question: A sign at the Kelowna community pool says the pool holds eight thousand forty litres of water. Which number matches those words?
questions.explain: ‘Forty’ means 4 tens, and nothing is said about hundreds, so a 0 holds the hundreds place: 8040. The classic trap is hearing ‘forty’ and writing 8400 — that would be read as eight thousand four hundred.

questions.question: A hiking map shows the length of a trail in expanded form as 5000 + 300 + 7 metres. What is this length in standard form?
questions.explain: Line the values up by place: 5 thousands, 3 hundreds, no tens, 7 ones, so the number is 5307. The trap is squeezing the digits together as 537 and forgetting that the empty tens place still needs a 0.

questions.question: Marcus is writing a fundraising cheque for his school and needs to write the amount $3506 in words. Which is correct?
questions.explain: Read the number by places — 3 thousands, 5 hundreds, 0 tens, 6 ones — which is three thousand five hundred six. Because the tens place is 0, you simply skip it; saying ‘sixty’ would mean 6 tens instead of 6 ones.

questions.question: A BC Ferries sailing report says 5072 passengers travelled to Nanaimo one Saturday. How should that number be written in words?
questions.explain: The digits are 5 thousands, 0 hundreds, 7 tens, 2 ones, so it reads five thousand seventy-two. The trap is treating the 7 as hundreds; with a 0 in the hundreds place, the 7 is only 7 tens.

questions.question: Jasmine's teacher reads out the number three thousand nine for a spelling-of-numbers quiz. Four students write it different ways. Which one is right?
questions.explain: After three thousand you hear no hundreds and no tens, so zeros must hold both of those places, giving 3009. Writing 3900 treats the 9 as hundreds, and 30009 comes from writing 3000 and then tacking a 9 on the end instead of placing it in the ones column.

questions.question: A Surrey school's read-a-thon total is posted in expanded form as 7000 + 90 + 3 pages. A student writes the word form as ‘seven thousand nine hundred three’. What is the correct word form?
questions.explain: The 90 in the expanded form is 9 tens, not 9 hundreds, so the number is 7093 and reads seven thousand ninety-three. Always match each part of the expanded form to its place — 90 is ninety and 900 would be nine hundred.

questions.question: A display at Science World says a model bridge is built from 3000 + 40 + 9 pieces. The label beside it must show the same amount in standard form and in word form. Which label is completely correct?
options: 3409 and three thousand four hundred nine
3049 and three thousand four hundred nine
questions.explain: 3000 + 40 + 9 has no hundreds, so the standard form is 3049 and it reads three thousand forty-nine — both parts must match. The trap is letting the 40 slide into the hundreds place and saying ‘four hundred’ when 40 means only 4 tens.

questions.question: Jordan is filling in a race form for the Vancouver Sun Run. The clerk says his participant number is four thousand twenty. Jordan hears each part and writes 4000, then writes 20 right after it. What should he have written in the box?
questions.explain: Four thousand twenty means 4 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens and 0 ones, so it goes in one four-digit box as 4020. Writing the parts one after another gives 400020, which is a much larger number — each digit has to land in its own place, not just follow the last one.
